data.name: Cecile
data.long_meaning: The name Cecile comes from the Hebrew word 'heqesel', which means 'grace' or 'beauty'. In the Bible, it is the name of a woman in the Old Testament who was favored by God and was called 'mother of all living'. In Christianity, Cecile is the name of several saints, including a third-century martyr and a sixth-century abbess.

in_hebrew.name: ססיל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם ססיל מקורו בשם העברי קהילה, שפירושו 'עוזרת לאלוהים' או 'שועלת לאל'. הוא קשור לשורש העברי 'קהל', שפירושו 'להתאסף' או 'להתקהל'. השם נמצא בשימוש בקרב קהילות יהודיות ונוצריות כאחד, ויש לו משמעות רוחנית עמוקה הקשורה ליחסים עם האל.

in_greek.name: Κεσίλ
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Κεσίλ είναι η ελληνική μορφή του ονόματος העברי קהילה (Qehillah), που σημαίνει 'βοηθός του Θεού' ή 'συντροφός του Θεού'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, το όνομα σχετίζεται με την έννοια της κοινότητας και της συντροφίας με τον Θεό. Το όνομα Κεσίλ έχει χρησιμοποιηθεί στην Εκκλησία των Ανατολικών Ρωμαίων και έχει πλούσιο ιστορικό και πνευματικό νόημα.

in_latin.name: Cecilia
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Cecilia is derived from the Latin word 'caecus', meaning 'blind'. It is associated with Saint Cecilia, a 2nd-century Roman martyr and patron saint of music. The name has been used in Christian tradition to signify spiritual blindness to worldly things and insight into divine truths. Cecilia is often invoked as a protector of musicians and artists.

historical_references.reference: Cecilia was a Roman noblewoman who was converted to Christianity in the 2nd or 3rd century. She was the daughter of a prominent Roman family and was betrothed to a pagan nobleman. When she revealed her Christian faith to him, he ordered her execution. Cecilia's body was miraculously healed after her death and she was venerated as a saint.

Saint Cecilia is also associated with music in Christian tradition. According to legend, while she was being taken to her execution, she sang hymns and played the organ so beautifully that the soldiers who were supposed to kill her were moved to tears and converted to Christianity.
